name: Temporal brow lift
lead: A temporal (lateral) brow lift raises the outer end of the eyebrow through incisions hidden in the hair of the temple. The outer third of the brow is the part that tends to droop first and most with age, and lifting it opens up the eye area, gives the brow a gentle upward arc and can make the upper eyelid look less heavy. [12][1]

It is one of several brow-lifting approaches, alongside coronal, endoscopic, direct, pretrichial and internal (transblepharoplasty) lifts, and it is often done together with upper blepharoplasty to prevent the brow from descending afterwards. [1][14][8] Non-surgical options that lift the lateral brow include botulinum toxin and filler to the temples. [2][15]

Evidence consists of surgical case series, comparative studies and one randomised trial of 32 women, and surgeons describe different variants with differing views on the best approach. [3][8][5][10] In looksmaxxing communities it is grouped with eye-area surgery, as a way to change the eye angle and the amount of visible upper lid. [16]

paras: Reviews of the ageing upper face describe the lateral third of the brow as ageing first and most, and note that brow shape depends heavily on the position of the lateral brow complex. [12] Surgeons add that attempts to elevate the brow often succeed medially but fail laterally, which led to techniques aimed at the lateral portion. [12]

Brow position was the main focus of aesthetic brow work in the late twentieth century, with the coronal lift the principal operation; more recently, brow shape has taken on greater importance and is addressed by endoscopic, temporal, direct and gliding approaches as well as non-surgical lifts, each with its own indications. [13] When upper blepharoplasty is done, a lateral brow lift is described as a necessary adjunct in some patients so the brow does not drop after the eyelid skin is removed. [14][8]

A skin-and-subcutaneous dissection through a temporal incision, which can be done under local anaesthesia, has been described for periorbital rejuvenation. [6] A temporal Z-incision technique for 37 patients was presented as simple and safe, with hidden scars and high satisfaction. [11] A 2026 article in Facial Plastic Surgery Clinics argues against the subcutaneous approach, and a 2026 Journal of Craniofacial Surgery report from one surgeon covering more than 500 consecutive lateral temporal subcutaneous lifts describes consistent, durable elevation and mostly temporary temporal numbness. [5][10]

Endoscopic lifts use small incisions and a camera. Because endoscopic brow lifts have a high reported recurrence rate, surgeons have described combining endoscopic and temporal approaches. [3] A 'modified lateral brow lift' hybrid uses small hidden incisions and deep-tissue fixation with features of an open technique. [12] Wikipedia describes endoscopic lifts as the most commonly used, with the coronal lift largely replaced. [1]
A 2015 study compared three different fixation techniques in temporal brow lift surgery. [7]

subs.h: Botulinum toxin and other non-surgical lifts
paras: A 2000 prospective case series of 22 patients found that botulinum toxin A directed at the brow depressors raised the brow, with the largest change at the lateral canthus, and the authors proposed it as an alternative to surgical brow elevation. A 2003 follow-up paper revisited the technique. [2][9][17] Wikipedia notes botulinum toxin effects are typically repeated every four to six months. [1] A registered trial (NCT07894822, completed, 36 participants) examined microfocused ultrasound, botulinum toxin and temporal hyaluronic acid filler together for non-surgical brow lifting. [19]

A retrospective review of endoscopic temporal brow lifts covering 2008 to 2018 included 159 brow lifts, 71 of them endoscopic temporal; mean elevation was about 1.8 to 1.9 mm at midpupil, medial canthus and lateral canthus, the complication rate was 1.4% and one relapse needed a repeat procedure, with mean follow-up around 7.6 months. [3][17]

A single-centre randomised trial of 32 women having upper blepharoplasty compared temporal brow lift with internal browpexy over six months and found no significant change in lateral brow position in the temporal lift group, while the internal browpexy group rose significantly; the authors favoured internal browpexy for long-term lateral stability. [8][17] Other work includes the subcutaneous temporal lift under local anaesthesia, a Z-lift series, and a fixation comparison. [6][11][7]
A cadaver study of 26 half-heads found the frontal branch of the facial nerve lies in the superficial fascia layer in the superolateral brow, defining the plane at risk in temporal dissection. [4]

Wikipedia states that complications of brow lifts are generally rare and minor in trained hands; hair loss is most associated with endoscopic lifts, numbness with direct lifts, and infection and bleeding are possible with any surgery. [1] The frontal branch of the facial nerve is the structure of concern in temporal dissection, and the single-surgeon series reports mostly temporary temporal numbness. [4][10] Recurrence, meaning the brow settling back down, is described for endoscopic lifts. [3]

Forum members raise lateral brow lifts when discussing the eye area, for example one poster who took photo edits to a plastic surgeon and was told the eyes in the edit could be reproduced with a lateral brow lift, then asked others whether the result might look unnatural. [16]

lore.intro: Lateral brow lifts come up on looksmax.org in eye-area threads and in surgery-planning questions, including after photo edits. [16]

claims.claim: A lateral brow lift can open up the eye area and change the eye angle.
claims.believers: Posters ask whether a lateral lift can reproduce the eye shape in a retouched photo. [16]
claims.experts: Surgical reviews describe the lateral brow as the part that ages first, and a retrospective review reported about 2 mm of mean elevation after endoscopic temporal lifts. [12][3]

claims.claim: A temporal lift is more durable than non-surgical options.
claims.believers: Users weigh surgery against injections that wear off. [16]
claims.experts: Botulinum toxin lifts are repeated every four to six months, per Wikipedia, while a randomised trial found little lateral change in the temporal group at six months compared with internal browpexy. [1][8]

claims.believers: One poster worried about looking 'funny' afterwards. [16]
claims.experts: Surgeons describe brow shape as more important than height and report techniques designed to keep a natural arc. [12]

card.summary: Surgical lateral eyebrow lift through temple incisions; documented in surgical series, with surgeon debate over technique.
card.note: Frontal branch facial nerve is the structure at risk; recurrence reported with some methods.

quick.overview:
A temporal brow lift raises the outer eyebrow through hidden incisions at the temples, sometimes with an endoscope.
Evidence is mostly surgical case series and technique comparisons; there are no large randomised trials.
quick.mechanism: Tissue at the brow tail is released and re-fixed higher at the temple, by subcutaneous, endoscopic or combined methods.
quick.risks: Reported risks include nerve injury, numbness, hair loss, infection, bleeding and recurrence of brow drop.

chain: Incision in the hair at the temple
Outer brow tissue is lifted and fixed higher
Brow tail sits higher and the upper eyelid looks more open
angle.text: The lift repositions the lateral brow upward, which shifts the shape of the eyebrow and the visible space between brow and lash line. People choose it to counter a drooping brow tail or to change how the eyes read in the face.
